newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power softer amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power softer amid mild weather.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished Tuesday softer than Monday's levels amid weather that continued to moderate from very cool temperatures this past weekend.
"It started to warm up a bit. There's a bit more surplus to sell," said a New York trader.
The 1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y., was boosting power toward full output by early Wednesday from its autumn refueling outage that began September 28.
With outlook of modest power demand, the outage of a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission power line from Quebec to New York was not a serious factor in today's trading.

The New York Power Authority (NYPA) shut two portions of the transmission line late last week. The segments of the entire line, which has a capacity to carry 2,350 MW of electricity, were expected to return to service Friday.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday delivery was assessed at $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Monday's range.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Wednesday was pegged in the $13.50-$14.50, compared with Monday's $14.00-$15.00 quote.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday was notationally valued at $27.00-$29.00, down from $29.00-$31.00 on Monday.
Off-peak, non-firm Tuesday electricity in eastern NYPP was again pegged at $16.00-$18.00, compared with Monday's quote near $17.00.
The 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear power station in Vernon, Vt., would resume full output some time today after more than a week's delay from its original startup from its refueling outage.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $31.00-$33.00, compared with a Monday's range of $32.00-$33.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $18.00-$19.50, against a quote of $18.00-$21.00 on Monday.
"Prices should go down more," said a Northeast marketer, but added the market could rebound when a Arctic cold blast descend from Canada this weekend.
